paper_metadata.title: Epilepsy surgery in children: Results and predictors of outcome on seizures

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the inclusion criteria and the baseline characteristics of the 113 children. However, it is a retrospective study from a single specialized center, and there is no information regarding the total number of eligible patients versus those actually included (participation rate), which introduces potential selection bias.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: 113 children (age at surgery under 16 years) with a postoperative followup of at least 2 years... operated on for medically refractory focal epilepsy at the "Claudio Munari" Epilepsy Surgery Center
items.reasoning: The population is clearly defined as pediatric patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy at a specific center.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: By retrospectively reviewing the records of the 492 patients operated on... from May 1996 to November 2004, we identified 113 children
items.reasoning: While the source (surgical records) is clear, the referral patterns and the flow of patients from initial evaluation to surgery are not detailed.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure freedom) was measured using the Engel Classification, which is the gold standard in epilepsy surgery research, and the follow-up duration was sufficient.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Outcome on seizures was assessed according to the Engel's classification (Engel et al., 1993).
items.reasoning: The Engel scale is a well-defined and validated outcome measure for epilepsy surgery.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome

items.evidence_snippet: mean, 55.1 months; SD, 24.8; range, 24–115
items.reasoning: The outcome is based on clinical follow-up over a significant period, which is standard for this field.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement

items.evidence_snippet: Outcome on seizures was assessed according to the Engel's classification... for reoperated patients, the outcome referred to the last procedure.
items.reasoning: A consistent classification was applied to all patients in the cohort.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the study uses multivariable logistic regression to adjust for confounders, the retrospective nature and the fact that 'tailored' surgery is itself a complex intervention mean that unmeasured surgical nuances or changes in medical management over the 8-year period might not be fully captured.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: Variables included... sex, neurologic status, age at seizure onset, duration of epilepsy, seizure frequency, MRI findings, use of VEEG and SEEG, age at surgery, type of surgery, side and site of surgery, extent of lesion resection, histology
items.reasoning: Most clinical and surgical variables are included, but specific details on postoperative antiepileptic drug (AED) changes—a major confounder—are not explicitly modeled.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: The site of surgical resection was categorized as a multinomial variable... Extent of lesion resection (complete or incomplete) was determined basing on operative reports, postoperative MRI
items.reasoning: The categories for surgical and clinical confounders are well-defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: MRI-based neuronavigation... routinely processed for histologic and immunohistochemical investigations
items.reasoning: Confounders like histology and lesion extent were measured using objective, high-quality methods.

items.evidence_snippet: All the patients received tailored microsurgical resections... at the "Claudio Munari" Epilepsy Surgery Center
items.reasoning: All data were collected within the same institutional framework.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical approach is sound, using bivariate analysis followed by multivariable logistic regression. The results are reported transparently with Odds Ratios and Confidence Intervals.

items.evidence_snippet: For bivariate analysis, Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test was used... and Fisher's two-tailed exact test... For multivariate analysis, three logistic regression models (with Wald test) were fitted
items.reasoning: The statistical plan is clearly outlined and appropriate for the data types.

items.label: Model development strategy

items.evidence_snippet: explanatory variables were selected according to the results of bivariate analysis and of best subsets technique, as well as to the main evidences of the literature.
items.reasoning: The model building combined statistical significance with clinical relevance.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
